conclusion.root_cause: Seed kernel passes all 9 official workloads but is grossly inefficient: each output element performs KD*KH*KW masked, data-dependent (non-affine) gather loads, so nothing vectorizes, and the host path adds autotune dispatch plus a redundant reshape/contiguous of the random samples. Prior trace showed a 90.8us device kernel for a 4096-output case, and full-call walltime of 1.55ms for the 131k-output timing-3 case, ~200x above the input-read bound.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Add an integer-ratio fast path: when alpha == kernel_size on every axis the pooling windows tile the input exactly, so start(od,oh,ow) = index*alpha and each program can read one fully contiguous input block, reshape it to [BH, AH, BW, AW] and reduce with a single NaN-aware max/argmax combine. Keep the seed's stride-aware gather kernel as the general fallback for non-integer ratios, drop input.contiguous() and the autotuner, and use one launch with a 3D grid.
